questions.question: Illustrate with example a real-world applications of the Control Process and outcome. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Illustrate with example a real-world application of the control process and outcome.
  • Ans: An example for a real-world application of the control process can be seen in a
  • manufacturing company’s quality control. The following are the steps:
  •  Step 1 Set standards: Limit the defective products to less than 2% of total production.
  •  Step 2 Measure performance: Inspection shows 5% of products are defective.
  •  Step 3 Compare: Deviation of 3% from the standard.
  •  Step 4 Corrective action: Adjust production process and retrain workers.
  • Outcome: Maintains product quality, reduces waste and ensures customer satisfaction.

questions.question: Distinguish between centralization and decentralization.
questions.solution_html:
• Distinguish between centralization and decentralization.
  • ● Centralisation
  • It means the concentration of power of decision making at one point or in a few
  • hands. In other words, all decisions and actions at lower level, require the sanction
  • of top management.
  • ● Decentralisation
  • It is the dispersal of decision making authority to lower levels. Top management
  • retains authority for overall control and coordination only in decentralisation
  • authority is pushed down to lower levels.

questions.question: Enumerate the factors of SWOT analysis. / [CO3, CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• Enumerate the factors of SWOT analysis.
  • Ans: SWOT analysis is a tool used to evaluate an organization’s internal and external
  • environment. It helps in strategic planning by identifying key factors that affect
  • performance. The factors are:
  •  Strengths – Strengths are the internal qualities or resources that helps the organization
  • to do better than its competitors, such as skilled employees, a strong brand or efficient
  • processes.
  •  Weaknesses – Weaknesses are the internal problems or areas where the organization
  • is weak, like old technology, poor infrastructure or lack of skills.
  •  Opportunities – Opportunities are the external factors that the organization can use to
  • its advantage, like new markets, new technology or changing customer needs.
  •  Threats – Threats are the external challenges or risks that can harm the organization,
  • such as competition, economic slowdowns or new regulations.
